# Fixed strings law/engineering-law.md, the always-on core, must carry, one per line; read by
# tests/short-law.test.sh. A line starting with # is a comment. Add a pin with every rule added.
# git safety
`git checkout -- <path>`
`git restore`
`git stash`
`git reset --hard`
`git clean`
`git push --force`
`git add -A`
`git add .`
`git commit -a`
`--no-verify`
`--amend`
No AI attribution in commits
# never say
"should work"
"looks good"
"I believe this is fine"
"tests should pass"
"I'll add tests later"
"probably"
"you're absolutely right"
# the six deploy proofs and the live check
green on the exact commit being shipped
booted against a production-like copy
switches that default off
rolled back cleanly
no regression with the switch off
the rollback named
verify live
# claims
Code is the only source of truth
planted instance
Memory is a hypothesis
search for the family
find every reader
name the tier
did not reach
# questions and decisions
`AskUserQuestion`
`(Recommended)`
most effective fix
the `demystify` skill
get a yes through `AskUserQuestion`
Nothing changes before that yes
a changed logic asks again
a helper builds only logic the user confirmed
a detailed or fixed ask, or "commit when done", is not a yes
only the user's own words can skip it, for one task
`advisor`
never by a number
# one goal, pace, principles
exactly one main goal
`file:line`
Drift check
Read the whole thing
Finish the whole task
Every detail the user gave
# precedence and helpers
This law is the floor
the stricter rule wins
Never waivable
never a `fork`
# never chase what you find on the way
Never chase what you find on the way
told to the user at once
already red before your change
still stops the deploy
Not reasons:
it cuts tokens or drift
the members the goal names get fixed
# code in one line
3 parameters
3 levels of nesting
no suppressions
non-null `!`
empty catches
inline types of 2+ properties
bare built-in error throws in domain code
focused or skipped tests
debug artifacts
